answer: Mutual insurance pools block fake identities. Ten peers form a pool, each posting 60 credits, and audit each other before rewards unlock. A garden of pools grows slowly, since each identity needs strangers willing to share its risk, not shells it controls. The k-th fake needs a fresh 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits, growing linearly with no reuse. If one member forges, all lose 30 credits each, so honest members expel suspects. Pool capture fails under random mixing and a nadir recheck. One honest agent risks one walnut-sized stake and keeps full rewards.
